summary: The formatter passes the existing hir/abap tests and handles common class and control-flow indentation. It still changes multiline template values, misreads nested templates, turns wrapped comments into code, and misses GET report events.

findings.claim: Indenting a continuation that is inside a multiline string template replaces its original leading spaces, changing the literal value instead of preserving it.
findings.repro:
abap.Format("CLASS z IMPLEMENTATION.
METHOD run.
DATA x TYPE string.
x = |first
  second|.
ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
") changes the two spaces before second to four; abaplint parses the input without errors.

findings.claim: The scanner treats the opening pipe of a nested string template as the end of the outer template, so a period and IF inside the nested literal create a false block and corrupt following indentation.
findings.repro:
abap.Format("CLASS z IMPLEMENTATION.
METHOD run.
DATA x TYPE string.
x = |{ |x. IF.| }|.
DATA y TYPE i.
ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
") emits six spaces before DATA y and four before ENDMETHOD; abaplint parses the input without errors.

findings.claim: Wrapping a full-line * comment writes its continuation without a comment marker, turning comment text into ABAP code and breaking Format idempotence.
findings.repro:
abap.Format("CLASS z IMPLEMENTATION.
METHOD run.
* " + strings.Repeat("comment ", 40) + "
DATA x TYPE i.
ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
") returns a second comment line beginning with "comment", not "*"; formatting that output again changes it.

findings.claim: GET logical-database report events are never recognized as event headers, leaving their bodies at column zero instead of two spaces.
findings.repro:
abap.Format("REPORT z.
GET node.
WRITE node-field.
FORM f.
WRITE 'x'.
ENDFORM.
") leaves WRITE node-field. unindented; abaplint parses GET node. as a Get statement.
